lyrics:
[Intro: acoustic guitar strum, plucked string stabs, light beat]

[Verse 1: warm, husky, conversational]
I am a sentence with the ending left off
A house with the paint still wet
Every year they ask me what I'm going to be
I haven't decided yet

[Pre-Chorus: bass enters, strings climb]
Staring at the cursor, blinking like a dare
Nobody else can put me there

[Chorus: full band, open, voice soars]
I'm still a first draft
Cross it out and start again
Ink on my fingers, sky in my head
No one's read the ending 'cause the ending isn't penned
Let the wind come through the pages
Let them turn
I'm still a first draft
And I'm good with that

[Verse 2: warm, a little bolder]
I've got chapters that I'd rather you would skip
A few I wrote in pencil, in a mood
There's a coffee ring on thirty-five
And a page where I was rude

[Pre-Chorus: bass and strings climb]
Staring at the margin, something I can't name
Nobody gets to hold the pen the same

[Chorus: full band, open, voice soars]
I'm still a first draft
Cross it out and start again
Ink on my fingers, sky in my head
No one's read the ending 'cause the ending isn't penned
Let the wind come through the pages
Let them turn
I'm still a first draft
And I'm good with that

[Bridge: gospel choir enters, handclaps, lead ad-libs]
(Not finished, not finished, not finished yet)
I've been waiting on a perfect line
(Not finished, not finished, not finished yet)
Turns out the messy ones are mine
(Not finished, not finished, not finished yet)

[Final Chorus: choir and lead together, key hits, tambourine]
I'm still a first draft
Cross it out and start again
Ink on my fingers, sky in my head
No one's read the ending 'cause the ending isn't penned
Let the wind come through the pages
Let them turn
I'm still a first draft
And I'm good with that

[Outro: choir alone, claps, a pen scratching]
(Not finished, not finished, not finished yet)
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 100 BPM, 4/4, F major. Easy, bright and steadily lifting. A walk that turns into a march with friends.

VOICE: Female, warm and a little husky, with an English accent audible in the vowels. Relaxed and conversational in the verses, open and strong in the chorus, improvising over the choir at the end. A gospel choir of mixed voices sings the bridge line and joins the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A steadily strummed acoustic guitar. Plucked and bowed string stabs in a hip-hop rhythm. A simple, crisp drum beat. Round bass. Handclaps and tambourine. Hammond-style organ under the choir. Light electric piano.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and string stabs. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Pre-chorus. 0:48 Chorus 1. 1:17 Verse 2. 1:41 Pre-chorus. 1:53 Chorus 2. 2:22 Bridge, the choir enters and repeats one line while the lead answers. 2:51 Final chorus with the choir. 3:20 Outro, the choir alone with claps, and the sound of a pen at 3:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2000s British pop-soul: clean, sunny and organic, acoustic guitar and strings up front, the choir wide and roomy.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The choir's entrance at 2:22.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original tells a teenager the page is blank. This singer has thirty-five pages with coffee rings on them and says the same thing about the rest. Being unfinished is the good news at any age.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Self-deprecation, acceptance, then celebration with company.
